model.rationale: Polls across a dozen October surveys show Talarico narrowly ahead, and his fundraising advantage plus the heavy outside spending against Paxton reinforce that edge; the state's Republican lean keeps the race close enough that a modest polling error would flip it.
model.watch: Early-voting turnout patterns or late consolidation of Republican-leaning voters behind Paxton could erase Talarico's narrow edge.
notes: Open seat: John Cornyn (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Texas's open Senate seat sits at the center of the midterm map. With John Cornyn not on the ballot, Republican Ken Paxton and Democrat James Talarico are competing for a seat that partisanship alone would tilt toward the GOP, but a favorable national environment and Paxton's polarizing profile have kept the race tight. Polls from mid-to-late October consistently show Talarico ahead by one to three points, with a few ties mixed in.

Talarico has raised far more money than Paxton and holds a large cash advantage, while outside groups have spent heavily against Paxton. Prediction markets give Talarico roughly a two-in-three chance, and most ratings place the race as a tossup, with a couple of outlets leaning Democratic. Early voting is underway, and both campaigns are crisscrossing the state in the final days.
